page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is an x86_64 memory-intensive server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core throughput. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0, supported by strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression at 34.8 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.37 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is more constrained, with a weak stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4441.07 and a weak bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 28.49 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for small, cached blocks at 345.37 GB/sec, but drops to a weaker 36.1 GB/sec for large, uncached blocks.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff, offering massive memory capacity and high single-core clock speeds at the expense of parallel processing power due to the low core count. This makes the FX8-4ms_v2 highly cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require massive multi-threaded CPU scaling. It is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for heavy multi-threaded workloads or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its poor text generation speed of 4.52 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.
